title: Garlic Butter Shrimp
subtitle: Twenty minutes, max flavor
description: Twenty minutes, max flavor. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

ingredients.name: Dry white wine or chicken broth

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Garlic Butter Shrimp in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch seafood. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep shrimp
steps.instruction: Pat shrimp completely dry with paper towels — moisture is the enemy of browning. Season with salt and pepper. Mince garlic and chop parsley. Have butter measured; this moves fast.

steps.title: Sear shrimp
steps.instruction: Heat a large skillet over medium-high until just smoking. Add 1 tbsp oil, then shrimp in a single layer (work in batches). Cook 60–90 seconds per side until pink with light browning. Remove immediately to a warm tray — do not overcook. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Garlic butter sauce
steps.instruction: Lower heat to medium. Add butter and garlic; swirl until butter foams and garlic smells sweet (30–45 seconds). Deglaze with wine or broth, scraping brown bits. Simmer 1 minute until slightly thickened. Return shrimp and any juices; toss to coat. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for fish, 145°F for shrimp until opaque. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Garlic Butter Shrimp onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Plate with lemon
steps.instruction: Finish with lemon juice, parsley, and red pepper flakes if using. Garlic Butter Shrimp should smell like butter and garlic, not fishy. Serve over rice, pasta, or with crusty bread on a warm tray — keep backup covered at 200°F for late calls so shrimp do not overcook.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Garlic Butter Shrimp — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Garlic Butter Shrimp with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Garlic Butter Shrimp on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Twenty minutes, max flavor. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Frozen shrimp is fine — thaw under cold running water and pat very dry.
